summary: The proposal contains several critical structural omissions and major methodological deficiencies, including missing mandatory sections, insufficient bibliography, and major figure shortcomings. While the writing displays some academic tone issues, the most urgent problems relate to compliance with required content, schedule violations, and missing AI transparency.

findings.title: Missing Introduction section
findings.description: The proposal does not contain an Introduction section, which is required by the guidelines.

findings.title: Missing Motivation section
findings.description: A dedicated Motivation section is required to present a visionary, positive outlook for solving the problem, but it is absent.

findings.title: Missing Objectives section
findings.description: The proposal lacks an Objectives section with a short introduction, a bullet list of high-level objectives, and detailed subsections for each objective, as required.

findings.title: Problem section contains solution statements
findings.description: The Problem section includes sentences that propose solutions, which should be omitted.

locations.quote: The CI server **should be migrated** to the VC server.
It **should be possible to adjust** the build plan after the task has been assigned.
In exams, it would be **useful to change** the student build plans after the submission date...

findings.title: Problem section does not identify actors
findings.description: The Problem section fails to explicitly name the stakeholders (e.g., instructors, students, universities) and describe how the problem negatively impacts them.

locations.quote: The interactive learning platform Artemis is an approach to use interactive learning during large computer science classes...

findings.title: Insufficient bibliography entries
findings.description: The bibliography contains only 5 entries, but the guidelines require at least 6‑8 peer‑reviewed publications.

locations.quote: References **[Booch95] ... [Gamma95] ... [Hilton16] ... [Krusche17] ... [Krusche18]**

findings.title: Missing AI Transparency Statement
findings.description: The proposal does not contain an AI transparency statement as required.

findings.title: Figures deficiency
findings.description: The proposal includes only one figure and lacks any required UML diagram, whereas the guidelines mandate at least two figures including a UML diagram.

findings.title: Figure not referenced in text
findings.description: Figure 1 is never cited in the surrounding text, violating the requirement that every figure be referenced.

findings.title: Paragraph length insufficient in multiple sections
findings.description: Paragraphs in the Abstract and Problem Statement are too short (1‑3 lines) and do not meet the required 5‑8 line length.

locations.quote: Motivation/Objective: **Since some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the efort required to maintain the servers and migrate the CI service from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service.**
Problem Statement: **The interactive learning platform Artemis currently only supports setups with an external CI server.   The CI server should be migrated to the VC server.      Furthermore, it**

Proposed Solution: **GitLab CI is the CI system provided by the GitLab VC server. This system supports the provision of the build plan via the Artemis API, which makes it possible to update the build plan retrospectively, as the build plan is fetched from the API on each run.**

(Expected) Results: **We expect to use the bridge pattern to dynamically bind Artemis to the concrete implementation with GitLab CI.      The reduction in server load will mean that more universities, especially smaller ones with less capacity, will choose Artemis.**

Artemis currently supports Bamboo      1 and Jenkins  2 as a CI server for executing the tests.   This leads to additional server overhead, since the CI and the Version Control (VC) are running on diferent servers.
Additionally, the base build plan is copied once after the student started the exercise [Krusche18].
the build plans must be updated manually in the CI Server.            Especially in large software engineering courses this is nearly impossible.

In exams, it would be useful to change the student build plans after the submission date to frstly hide the test cases during the exam and only compile the code and secondly use a debug compiler not failing due to a simple syntax error.

findings.title: Paragraph mixes unrelated ideas
findings.description: A single paragraph in the Related Work section discusses unrelated concepts (Booch, Fowler, Krusche et al.) together, violating the one‑idea‑per‑paragraph rule.

locations.quote: According to Grady Booch’s book Object-oriented analysis and design with applications integration should generally take place regularly, to avoid problems later on [Booch95].       Martin Fowler explains in his post  Continuous    Integration,  Continuous   Integration  as  a practice,  in which   each integration,  which **should take place at least once per day per developer, is build and tested with predefned test cases**.   In their paper Interactive Learning – Increasing Student Participation through Shorter Exercise Cycles, Krusche et al. have taken up this concept to improve the learning experience in large computer science courses at university [Krusche17].

findings.title: Enumerated list used instead of prose in System Requirements
findings.description: The System Requirements and Top Level Design section presents the workflow as a numbered list, which is not allowed outside of schedule or objective sections.

findings.title: Passive voice usage
findings.description: Passive constructions are used; revise to active voice.

locations.quote: The **CI server should be migrated** to the VC server.
the base build plan **is copied** once after the student started the exercise.
Later changes to the base build plan **are not patched** automatically to all student build plans, but rather the build plans **must be updated** manually in the CI Server.

findings.title: Excessive filler words and superlatives
findings.description: Filler words and superlatives such as 'Furthermore', 'Additional', 'Very' dilute academic tone; remove or replace.

locations.quote: **Furthermore**, it should be possible to adjust the build plan after the task has been assigned.
This leads to **additional** server overhead, since the CI and the Version Control (VC) are running on different servers.
**Additionally**, the base build plan is copied once after the student started the exercise.
**Furthermore**, the CI service should be part of the VC server to reduce **additional** efort by maintaining two servers.
The current setup and implementation makes it **very** cumbersome to update the build plan afterwards.

findings.title: Forbidden sentence starters
findings.description: Sentences start with prohibited words (Since, To, As, etc.); rewrite to avoid.

locations.quote: **Since** some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the effort required...
**To** achieve this goal, Artemis uses a Version Control (VC) and Continuous Integration (CI) server...

**Since** the benefts of using CI are quite high and nearly half of the developers who do not use CI mention a lack of familiarity as the reason for not using a CI service, it is useful to teach the concepts of CI at university.
**As** a result, instructors are able to update the build plan after the release of an exercise, GitLab CI fetches the updated build plan when needed.
**As** described in section 3, this might lead to better developers and better code...

findings.description: The proposal uses both “CI server” and “CI service” to refer to the same Continuous Integration component, leading to inconsistency.

findings.title: Waterfall‑style schedule, not agile
